figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Posterior accuracy. CD-PFN’s PIPs against exact PIPs under the linear $g$-prior for 3011 covariates across 300 datasets, before (left) and after (right) fine-tuning on that prior. The dotted line marks equality.
figures.headline: Fine-tuning moves CD-PFN's posterior inclusion probabilities much closer to exact values, reducing mean absolute error from 0.19 to 0.03.
citing_sentences: Figure 1 compares CD-PFN’s PIPs with exact PIPs on 300 unseen datasets from this prior, before and after two hours of fine-tuning.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Ranking accuracy. Mean AUPRC over 100 trials as $n$, $p$, and $\lvert S\rvert$ vary from the baseline ($n=250$, $p=200$, $\lvert S\rvert=10$), for each dataset and response type.
figures.headline: CD-PFN has the highest mean area under the precision-recall curve as sample size, covariates, and active covariates vary from baseline.
citing_sentences: CD-PFN has the highest AUPRC in all 30 settings, exceeding the next best method by more than two standard errors in 28 (Figures 2, S7, S8, S9, S10, and S11).

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: FDR-based selection. TPR (top) and empirical FDR (bottom) against the target FDR, averaged over 100 trials at the baseline simulation parameters. The dotted line marks an empirical FDR equal to the target; a method controls FDR if its empirical FDR curve lies at or below this line.
figures.headline: At baseline settings, methods are compared on true positive rate only where their empirical false discovery rate stays at or below target.
citing_sentences: Among the methods whose empirical FDR is at most the target level of 0.1, CD-PFN has the highest TPR in 20 settings (Figures 3, S13, S14, S15, and S16).

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: NHANES selections with age and sex as the response. Covariates selected at target FDR level 0.1 with age (top) or sex (bottom) as the response. Arrows out of the response are children and arrows into it are parents. Since no measurement can cause age or sex, red arrows are errors. AVICI, which selects nothing, is omitted.
figures.headline: With age and sex as responses, each other method selects some measurements as causes of age or sex, which no measurement can be.
citing_sentences: Figure 4 shows the selections with age and sex as the response.
Table S24 gives the results, and Figure 4 shows each method’s selections with age and sex as the response.

figures.label: Figure S1
figures.caption: Fine-tuning loss. Cross-entropy loss of CD-PFN’s conditional dependence output during fine-tuning on the linear $g$-prior, on training batches (gray) and on 512 fixed validation datasets (red).
figures.headline: Fine-tuning loss falls most in the first minute of training on the linear g-prior, on both training batches and validation datasets.
citing_sentences: Interestingly, most of the reduction in loss comes in the first minute of training (Figure S1).
Figure S1 shows this loss over the two hours of fine-tuning.

figures.label: Figure S2
figures.caption: Ways a covariate can be conditionally dependent on the response. A structural causal model with covariates $X_{1},\dots,X_{7}$ and a latent variable $L$; dashed nodes are unobserved, and $X_{6}$ is a coarse measurement of $\tilde{X}_{6}$. Shaded covariates are conditionally dependent on $Y$ given the others. $X_{2}$ is a parent, as is $X_{6}$ through its underlying variable $\tilde{X}_{6}$; $X_{3}$ is a child, and $X_{4}$ another parent of that child. $X_{1}$ shares the unobserved cause $L$ with $Y$, and $X_{5}$ acts through $\tilde{X}_{6}$, which is observed only coarsely; neither is a parent or a child. $X_{7}$ is not conditionally dependent on $Y$, because its only path to $Y$ passes through the observed $X_{2}$.
figures.headline: Covariates depend on the response as parents, children, or latent-cause partners, but not solely through observed parents.
citing_sentences: Figure S2 illustrates the ways a covariate can be conditionally dependent on the response, and Section S5.3 gives additional details.
Figure S2 illustrates the resulting conditional dependence labels.

figures.label: Figure S3
figures.caption: Examples of the functions $g_{j}$. Standardized functions $\tilde{g}_{j}$ of eight TCGA covariates in one sample of 250 observations, with bumpy (top) and smooth (bottom) length-scales. Dotted lines mark the 5th and 95th percentiles of the covariate, beyond which the effect flattens, and ticks at the bottom mark the observed values.
figures.headline: Simulated covariate effects are bumpy or smooth depending on length-scale, and flatten beyond the 5th and 95th percentiles.
citing_sentences: Figure S3 shows examples of the functions $g_{j}$, and Section S6.2 gives the full construction.
Length-scales are drawn with equal probability from $\operatorname{Unif}(1,1.5)$ or $\operatorname{Unif}(3,5)$, producing bumpy or smooth effects (Figure S3).

abstract: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) have become state-of-the-art for tabular prediction but remain underexplored in other areas of statistics. In this work, we present two PFNs for Bayesian variable selection: CD-PFN identifies conditional dependencies, and PC-PFN identifies parents and children in a causal graph. Both networks estimate posterior inclusion probabilities (PIPs) without posterior samples or data-specific modeling. In semi-synthetic and real data experiments, CD-PFN and PC-PFN often outperform existing methods, demonstrating the value of PFNs for variable selection and their potential in statistics more broadly. Open-source software is available.

sections.body:
Bayesian variable selection reports a posterior inclusion probability (PIP) for each covariate, but computing PIPs usually requires a likelihood and posterior inference on each dataset. The authors train transformers on data simulated from a prior, so each new dataset needs only a forward pass. CD-PFN estimates whether each covariate is conditionally dependent on the response. PC-PFN estimates whether each covariate is a parent or child of the response.

In a preview with 50 trials of n=100 samples and p=50 gene-expression covariates, CD-PFN performs best in both nonlinear settings and nearly matches linear spike-and-slab on linear responses (Table 1). CD-PFN computes all 50 PIPs in 0.2 seconds on a CPU. TabPFN with permutation importance is over a thousand times slower, because it needs over a thousand predictions per dataset.
sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.headline: CD-PFN performs best in both nonlinear simulated settings and nearly matches linear spike-and-slab on linear responses, without tuning.

sections.body:
The networks estimate a binary parameter's posterior probability by minimizing a loss on simulated datasets. Proposition 2.1 shows that this loss is minimized exactly when the network output equals the posterior probability. CD-PFN gives one PIP per covariate, and PC-PFN gives two per covariate, one for parent and one for child.

PIPs are turned into selections by controlling the posterior expected false discovery proportion at a chosen level. The authors note that this control is approximate in practice, since the networks produce approximate PIPs. The networks are transformers that alternate attention across observations and covariates. Fine-tuning CD-PFN on a linear regression prior with exact PIPs reduced mean absolute error from 0.19 to 0.03.
sections.heading: 2. PFNs for variable selection
sections.headline: Training with binary cross-entropy on simulated data targets the posterior probability itself, so no posterior sampling is needed.

sections.body:
Table 2 summarizes the priors. CD-PFN draws from the X-first class with probability 0.75 and from structural causal models with probability 0.25. PC-PFN uses X-first with probability 0.425, structural causal models with probability 0.425, and linear Gaussian structural causal models with probability 0.15. The response is continuous with probability 0.7 and binary with probability 0.3. Sample size ranges from 16 to 1024. The number of covariates is 8 to 256 with probability 0.8 and 257 to 512 with probability 0.2.

Covariates may be parents of the response, children of it, or share an unobserved cause with it. The authors state that likelihood-based inference for these relations would need a joint model with latent variables and unknown causal directions. A PFN only needs to simulate from such a model.
sections.heading: 3. Priors
sections.headline: The priors mix an X-first class with structural causal models, covering covariates that are effects of the response or share latent causes with it.

sections.body:
The simulations draw data from kidney cancer gene expression and from the Bioresponse dataset. Each experiment has 100 trials. The response is a sum of Gaussian process functions of a random subset of covariates, with continuous or binary outcomes. The baseline is n=250, p=200, and 10 active covariates, and 30 settings are varied across the datasets and response types.

CD-PFN has the highest AUPRC in all 30 settings. Its empirical false discovery rate is below target at levels 0.05 and 0.1 in all 30 settings, and it has the highest true positive rate among methods within target in 20. On a simulated linear Gaussian DAG, BiDAG ranks best, while PC-PFN selects conservatively with a lower true positive rate. The authors do not evaluate TabPFN or BKMR here because of their computational cost.
sections.heading: 4. Simulation studies
sections.headline: Across simulations, CD-PFN ranks covariates best in all 30 settings and PC-PFN ranks parents and children best in all nine gene expression settings.

sections.body:
The biomarker tasks use nine TCGA tumor-status tasks and 23 cancer cell line tasks, with 456 or 504 panel genes. CD-PFN selects 15 of 18 established biomarkers in tasks with several, against at most 13 for other methods. In single-biomarker tasks it selects 21 of 25, while spike-and-slab, SuSiE, and IPSS select 22 or 23 with two to four times as many other selections.

For metabolic syndrome in NHANES, CD-PFN selects 5.8 of seven defining variables on average over 20 samples of 1000 participants, against 4.5 for spike-and-slab and 4.3 for SuSiE. PC-PFN gives the correct direction for all 45 selections involving age, sex, or ethnicity. In the light tunnel experiment, PC-PFN ranks children best, and no method selects children reliably.
sections.heading: 5. Real data
sections.headline: CD-PFN selects 15 of 18 established biomarkers in multi-biomarker tasks, and PC-PFN orients all 45 demographic selections correctly.

sections.body:
The discussion identifies two directions. The first is how the prior affects performance. A broad prior gives a general-purpose model, while substantive knowledge may justify a narrower class. Fine-tuning CD-PFN on a linear regression prior substantially improved its accuracy under that prior. Open questions include how much simulated data is needed and which parts of a pretrained model to fine-tune.

The second direction is that the framework applies to any binary parameter, not only conditional dependence, parents, and children. The authors also report preliminary results that CD-PFN and PC-PFN extrapolate to sample sizes and dimensions larger than any seen in training.
sections.heading: 6. Discussion
sections.headline: The authors propose studying how priors shape performance, adapting networks to new priors, and extending the framework to other binary targets.

sections.body: The `varselpfn` package and trained networks can be installed with `pip install varselpfn` and are available from a GitHub repository. Code that reproduces all results is in a separate GitHub repository, and saved results are archived on Zenodo. All datasets are publicly available from their original sources.
sections.heading: Code and data availability
sections.headline: The varselpfn package, trained networks, and reproduction code are publicly available, and all datasets come from public sources.

sections.body: The appendix compares amortized selection methods in Table S1 and gives the preview simulation setup. It covers network dimensions and training, the exact posterior setup for the g-prior check, and the prior construction and mechanism families. It also gives real-data details for the biomarker tasks, the metabolic syndrome study using the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), the NHANES direction checks in Table S24, and the light tunnel experiment.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists related methods, setup and architecture details, prior construction, and real-data specifics for the biomarker, survey, and light tunnel studies.
